title: What was refused?
description:
An access mask is a set of bits, one per right. When an open fails, a helpful tool tells the user which rights were missing. Write two functions.

- `missingRights(requested, granted)` returns the bits that are in `requested` but not in `granted`.
- `rightNames(mask)` returns the names of the process rights set in `mask`, in the order of this table, and appends `"other"` once if any bit not in the table is set.

| Name | Bit value |
|---|---|
| `terminate` | `0x0001` |
| `create_thread` | `0x0002` |
| `vm_operation` | `0x0008` |
| `vm_read` | `0x0010` |
| `vm_write` | `0x0020` |
| `query_information` | `0x0400` |
| `query_limited_information` | `0x1000` |
| `synchronize` | `0x100000` |

```
missingRights(0x1010, 0x1000)  = 0x0010
rightNames(0x1010)             = { "vm_read", "query_limited_information" }
```
hints: "In `requested` but not in `granted`" is `requested & ~granted`: `~` flips every bit of `granted`, so the AND keeps only the bits it lacks.
For the names, go through a table of bit and name in order, testing `mask & bit`. Build up a mask of all known bits as you go; anything left in `mask & ~known` is "other".
lessonTitle: Access Rights, Tokens and Why Windows Says No
